_note: Quest content (rules/quests.ts). quests: the journal — summary (one line), stages (stage id → where things stand, in order) and tips (stage id → the short next step; past steps show ticked); dialogs: conversations (entry picks the first node whose condition holds); hooks: where content attaches — "<location>/<building spot name>" buttons, or "site:<id>" on the world map (fires on arrival or when the party bumps into a blocking site); sites: blocking and icons for world-map sites (positions in world.json, type site); triggers: fire once when their condition becomes true. Quest progress is the flag quest:<id> (stage, "none" before it starts, "done" at the end). Fights scale to the party (party size − 1, rules/scaling.ts); a fight action may override the difficulty and tweak monsters.

tips.accepted: Clear the rats out of the Shrine of the Dawn — Mother Ilse will let you in.
tips.cleared: Tell Reeve Tamsin in her hall.

stages.accepted: Reeve Tamsin Holt wants the rats cleared out of the Shrine of the Dawn, south-west of Millbrook's market. Mother Ilse will let you in.
stages.cleared: The shrine is quiet at last. Tell the reeve in her hall.
stages.done: The Shrine of the Dawn is open again, and the reeve paid 25 gp.

ale.name: Dry Taps
ale.summary: The Leaky Bucket has run out of ale.

tips.find-brewery: Find the brewery in the hills north-west of Millbrook.
tips.find-parts: Search the old shack east of Millbrook, by the river, for brewing parts.
tips.return-parts: Bring the spigot parts to Brewmaster Odo at the brewery.

stages.find-brewery: The Leaky Bucket has no ale: the brewery stopped sending barrels. The innkeeper thinks it lies in the hills to the north-west of Millbrook.
stages.find-parts: Brewmaster Odo's main spigot has cracked and he can't pay the smith. He thinks an old shack to the east, by the river, may still hold brewing parts.
stages.return-parts: You found some old spigot parts in the shack. Take them back to Odo at the brewery — who knows if they work.
stages.done: The ale flows again. The Leaky Bucket sells it by the mug.

troll.name: The Troll Toll
troll.summary: A troll holds the broken bridge to the east.

tips.met: Get past the troll: fight it at level 3, soften it with ale — or tempt it away with a drier home full of rats.

stages.met: A troll has torn up the old bridge over the river and squats there with its rats. Nobody crosses east. Fighting it is deadly below level 3 — perhaps there is another way.
stages.done: The troll is gone and Millbrook's carpenters have mended the bridge. The road east is open.

meet.text: The ground shudders. An ogre lumbers out of the rocks, dragging a club the size of a tree trunk, and sniffs the air in your direction.

slipped.text: You flatten yourselves among the boulders. The ogre grumbles, scratches, and stomps off up the hill.

caught.text: It bellows and swings round to face you. Too late to hide.

meet.text: "That's far enough." Figures step out from behind the trees on both sides of the road, blades drawn. Their captain smiles. "Purses on the ground, and nobody bleeds."

slipped.text: You back into the brush and circle wide. By the time they've searched the ditch you're long gone.

caught.text: An arrow thuds into the road at your feet. "Wrong answer."

meet.text: Mist curls across the barrow-mounds. Grey shapes rise out of it — bones that should have stayed buried, and things that still hunger.

slipped.text: You hold your breath and keep low. The dead shamble past, blind to all but the warmth they can't find.

caught.text: A skull turns toward you with a dry click. They've found you.

meet.text: Bones scrape on stone somewhere ahead. Out of the dark they come — the keep's old dead, roused by your footsteps.

slipped.text: You press into a niche and let them shuffle by into the dark.

caught.text: A cold hand closes on your sleeve. No hiding now.

meet.text: Squealing erupts from the long grass. A pack of giant rats, mangy and bold, comes boiling toward you.

slipped.text: You melt back into cover and wait. After a while they lose interest and move on.

caught.text: A twig snaps underfoot. They've seen you — no way out now.

meet.text: Leathery wings beat overhead. Giant bats swoop down out of the trees, and something scurries in the undergrowth below.

slipped.text: You melt back into cover and wait. After a while they lose interest and move on.

caught.text: A twig snaps underfoot. They've seen you — no way out now.

meet.text: A web glistens between two trunks — and then its owners move. Giant wolf spiders, big as dogs, come skittering out.

slipped.text: You melt back into cover and wait. After a while they lose interest and move on.

caught.text: A twig snaps underfoot. They've seen you — no way out now.

hello.speaker: Reeve Tamsin Holt
hello.text: Rats! Rats in the granary, rats in the well — and now rats in the Shrine of the Dawn. The priests are sleeping at the inn. Clear the shrine and the town will pay you twenty-five gold.

thanks.speaker: Reeve Tamsin Holt
thanks.text: Bless you. Mother Ilse waits at the shrine door — tell her I sent you. Mind the crypt: that's where they nest.

waiting.speaker: Reeve Tamsin Holt
waiting.text: The shrine is still crawling, I hear. The crypt below the altar is the worst of it.

reward.speaker: Reeve Tamsin Holt
reward.text: Quiet as a tomb, Mother Ilse says — the good kind of quiet. Here, as promised. Millbrook won't forget it.

chat.speaker: Reeve Tamsin Holt
chat.text: A troll has taken the old bridge east of here and torn half of it into the river. Nobody crosses. I'd not go near it unless you're seasoned — level three at the least. And the inn has run dry, which is making everyone surly.

chat-open.speaker: Reeve Tamsin Holt
chat-open.text: The road east is open again, thanks to you. Fenwick's traders are already at the market.

closed.speaker: Mother Ilse
closed.text: You can't go in there, friend. Too many rats — they bite, and they're bold as wolves. If you want to help, speak to the reeve in her hall.

open.speaker: Mother Ilse
open.text: The reeve sent you? The Dawn be thanked. They're in the nave, and worse down in the crypt behind the altar. I'll bar the door behind you.

cleared.speaker: Mother Ilse
cleared.text: You did it! I'll light the candles again. Do tell the reeve.

tend.speaker: Mother Ilse
tend.text: You did it — and paid dearly for it, I see. Bring your fallen to the altar. The Dawn owes you this much.

tended.speaker: Mother Ilse
tended.text: Rest now, and tell the reeve the shrine is ours again. The candles will burn for you tonight.

dry.speaker: Marta Pennyfeather, innkeeper
dry.text: No ale, I'm afraid — not a drop. The brewery up in the hills stopped sending barrels two weeks back, and nobody's been to see why. Somewhere north-west of town, it is; I've never been. If you find out what's wrong, there's a free round in it.

thanks.speaker: Marta Pennyfeather, innkeeper
thanks.text: Bless you. Follow the hills north-west — you'll smell it before you see it.

waiting.speaker: Marta Pennyfeather, innkeeper
waiting.text: Still dry. My regulars are drinking well water and complaining about it, and Merle has taken to hiding in the cellar.

flowing.speaker: Marta Pennyfeather, innkeeper
flowing.text: Listen to that — a full room again! Merle's rolling barrels up from the cellar as fast as his back allows. Ale's four copper a mug, and the first one's on the house.

found.speaker: Odo, brewmaster
found.text: Visitors! Don't tell me — Marta sent you. It's the main spigot: split clean down the middle. Can't draw a barrel without it, and the smith wants more than I'll see this season. There's an old shack east of here, by the river — the last brewer kept his spare fittings there. Might be something left, if the vermin haven't had it.

waiting.speaker: Odo, brewmaster
waiting.text: The shack's east of here, by the river. Mind the bats — they nest in the roof.

parts.speaker: Odo, brewmaster
parts.text: Let's see… brass, a bit green, but — yes! This'll seat. Give me an hour.

fixed.speaker: Odo, brewmaster
fixed.text: Hear that gurgle? Sweetest sound in the Vale. I can't pay you — every copper I have is in those vats — but the Leaky Bucket will have barrels by nightfall. Drink one for me.

thanks-again.speaker: Odo, brewmaster
thanks-again.text: Spigot's holding! Tell Marta I said hello.

closed.text: The brewery is shut and quiet.

found.text: Behind a wall of brambles you find a sagging shack. The door hangs by one hinge. Inside, something squeaks — a lot of somethings — and leathery wings stir in the rafters.

onWin.say: Among the droppings and broken crates you find old brewing gear and a few things somebody left behind.

empty.text: The old shack is empty but for droppings and broken crates.

troll-home.speaker: The troll
troll-home.text: The troll sits in the shack's doorway, crunching something that squeaked not long ago. It sees you and waves a huge claw. "Friend! Shack dry. Rats tasty. Troll happy."

choices.text: Ask if it has found anything around here.
Ask about the old brewing gear inside.
Share a mug of ale with it.

troll-gear.speaker: The troll
troll-gear.text: "Rats in shack. Bats in shack. Troll eat." It pats its belly, then shoves a crate of junk out of the door with one foot. "Not food. Friend take." Among the junk: old brewing gear and a few things somebody left behind.

gift.speaker: The troll
gift.text: The troll rummages under a heap of bones and holds out a sodden purse. "Shiny. Troll no eat shiny. Friend take."

cheers.speaker: The troll
cheers.text: The troll drains the mug in one gulp, thumps its chest and bellows a song with no tune and only one word: "RATS!" Birds flee for half a mile.

choices.text: Applaud, and leave while your ears still work.

meet.speaker: The troll
meet.text: A troll heaves itself up from the end of the bridge, rats boiling around its feet. Behind it, the middle of the bridge is gone. "Toll," it rumbles. "Toll is: YOU."

choices.text: Tell it about the old shack by the river — dry, quiet, plenty of rats to eat.
Offer it a mug of ale.

onWin.say: The troll crashes into the river and does not get up. Millbrook's carpenters come out to mend the bridge.

persuaded.speaker: The troll
persuaded.text: The troll scratches its head with a claw. "Dry? Rats?" It sniffs the air toward the north, grunts, and wades off upstream without a backward glance. Its rats are not so easily convinced.

onWin.say: With the troll gone, Millbrook's carpenters come out to mend the bridge.

refused.speaker: The troll
refused.text: "Lies," the troll growls, and spits. "Troll stay. Troll eat."

choices.text: Offer it a mug of ale.

onWin.say: The troll crashes into the river and does not get up. Millbrook's carpenters come out to mend the bridge.

drunk.speaker: The troll
drunk.text: The troll snatches the mug, sniffs, and pours it down in one gulp. Then it belches, sways, and grins. "More!" It is in no state to aim straight — but it is still in the way.

choices.text: While it's merry, tell it about the old shack by the river — dry, quiet, plenty of rats.

onWin.say: The troll crashes into the river and does not get up. Millbrook's carpenters come out to mend the bridge.

merry-refused.speaker: The troll
merry-refused.text: The troll laughs so hard it nearly falls off the bridge. "Funny! Troll stay. More ale!" It still sways on its feet.

onWin.say: The troll crashes into the river and does not get up. Millbrook's carpenters come out to mend the bridge.

hooks.label: Buy a mug of ale (4 cp)

do.say: The party shares a mug of Odo's ale. It is cool, bitter and very welcome.
The last rat squeals and lies still. The Shrine of the Dawn is quiet.
Mother Ilse is waiting at the shrine door. Speak with her before you go — she will tend your fallen.
Word reaches the Leaky Bucket fast: Marta puts a mug of ale aside for you.
